finding.title: Bootstrap admin password lifecycle broken: ADMIN_PASSWORD silently ignored after first boot, compose default suppresses the weak-password warning, and the DB file outside the volume reverts the password to admin123 on container recreation
finding.evidence: main.go:164-169 `func bootstrapAdmin(gdb *gorm.DB, cfg *config.Config) { var count int64; gdb.Model(&model.AdminUser{}).Count(&count); if count > 0 { return } }` — with users present, ADMIN_PASSWORD is dropped with no log line. main.go:170-174 `pass := cfg.AdminPassword; if pass == "" { pass = "admin123"; log.Println("[bootstrap] WARNING: using default admin password 'admin123'. Set ADMIN_PASSWORD to change.") }` — the warning is gated on the empty string, yet docker-compose.yml:18 always injects a value: `- ADMIN_PASSWORD=${ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin123}` (.env.template:28 also ships `ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin123` uncommented), so under the documented deployment pass is never empty and the WARNING never fires even though admin123 is used. Persistence: config.go:62 `DBDSN: getenv("DB_DSN", "gateway.db")` is relative, resolved against Dockerfile:25 `WORKDIR /app` (= /app/gateway.db), while docker-compose.yml:26 mounts only `${DATA_DIR_PATH:-./data}:/app/data`.
finding.impact: Three compounding silent effects. (1) An operator who boots with the compose default, is told to change the password, later sets a strong ADMIN_PASSWORD and restarts keeps admin123 forever — the env var is simply unused, with no warning or error. (2) A default docker-compose deployment logs NOTHING about admin123 while README:56 asserts the default password is announced on the console, so nobody learns the console is reachable with a published credential on 0.0.0.0 (compose:10 `${PORT:-8080}:8080`). (3) Because the SQLite file is not in the volume, any container re-creation wipes the account and re-bootstraps it with the compose value — an admin who rotated away from admin123 is transparently rotated BACK to the published default, the only trace being main.go:183 `[bootstrap] created admin user: admin`. With authn-3/authn-4 (no login throttling) and authn-6 (MFA not enforced) a known credential is total compromise of the gateway and all upstream provider keys.
finding.mitigations_checked: the password is bcrypt-hashed at creation (main.go:175, DefaultCost) and compared with the constant-time library helper; ADMIN_USER uniqueness is enforced (`gorm:"uniqueIndex"`, model.go:15); PUT /auth/password exists (routes.go:45) so rotation is possible; no API returns the default password. None of these address the silent-ignore / silent-restore behaviour.
finding.recommendation: Require ADMIN_PASSWORD (`ADMIN_PASSWORD=${ADMIN_PASSWORD:?...}`) or generate a random one printed once; log an ERROR (and optionally refuse /api/admin/v1) when a login succeeds with the default literal; make bootstrap reconcile ADMIN_USER/ADMIN_PASSWORD with the DB or explicitly log 'ADMIN_PASSWORD ignored: N users already exist'; default DB_DSN into the mounted volume (e.g. /app/data/gateway.db); force a password change on first login for accounts still on the default.

reason: The finding survives adversarial review: every quote was re-read in the cited files and is verbatim-accurate, and the exploit chain closes at every step. CORRECTED ANCHOR: the cited line 166 is `gdb.Model(&model.AdminUser{}).Count(&count)`; the ignore itself is decided on main.go:167-168 (`if count > 0 {` / `return`), so 167 is the precise line. SUB-CLAIM A (ADMIN_PASSWORD silently ignored) — CONFIRMED. main.go:164-169 returns before touching cfg.AdminPassword once any admin row exists. Whole-repo grep shows `AdminPassword` has exactly one producer (config.go:66 `AdminPassword: os.Getenv("ADMIN_PASSWORD")`) and exactly one consumer (main.go:170), so there is no reconcile/rotate path anywhere else; warnInsecureDefaults (main.go:187-194) checks only JWT_SECRET and MASTER_KEY and never the admin credential. There is also no admin-provisioning API to fall back on: routes.go:133-135 expose only GET /users, POST /users/:id/unbind-mfa, POST /users/:id/unlock, and PUT /auth/password requires the OLD password (auth.go:176 `bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(u.PasswordHash), []byte(req.OldPassword))`). Bootstrap is therefore the single entry point for the only credential in the system. SUB-CLAIM B (compose default suppresses the warning) — CONFIRMED. main.go:171 `if pass == ""` is the only trigger for the admin123 WARNING, and docker-compose.yml:18 `- ADMIN_PASSWORD=${ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin123}` makes pass non-empty on every `docker compose up`, so the branch at main.go:172-173 is dead code in the documented Docker path even though admin123 is exactly what is written (main.go:175/179). README.md:56 ('First boot auto-creates the admin user ... and prints the default password to the console') and quickstart.en.md:47 ('Default account `admin` / `admin123` (when `ADMIN_PASSWORD` is unset; startup logs print a WARNING)') promise an alert that provably never fires. SUB-CLAIM C (DB outside the volume) — CONFIRMED as a config fact. config.go:62 defaults DB_DSN to the relative path `gateway.db`; docker-compose.yml:14 re-injects that same default; db.go:27 `dialector = sqlite.Open(dsn)` passes it through unchanged to the pure-Go driver, so it resolves against the process CWD, which is Dockerfile:25 `WORKDIR /app` → /app/gateway.db; docker-compose.yml:26 mounts only `${DATA_DIR_PATH:-./data}:/app/data`. On container re-creation db.go:63 AutoMigrate rebuilds an empty schema and bootstrapAdmin runs again → the live credential becomes the compose value, traceable only by main.go:183. Exposure and lack of second factor were verified: docker-compose.yml:10 `"${PORT:-8080}:8080"` publishes on all host interfaces, and a bootstrapped account is protected by password alone because auth.go:86 gates the second step on `sec.MFAEnabled && u.MFAEnabled` (a fresh row has MFAEnabled=false) while settings.go:87 DefaultSecurity() ships `MFARequiredAll: false`, so issueLogin (auth.go:110 → 124-138) mints a fully privileged JWT. The 5-failure/15-minute lockout (auth.go:113-122) is irrelevant against a published credential. NOT AVOIDED BY DOCUMENTATION ALONE: the first-boot-only semantics are stated (.env.template:25 '仅首次启动建号时生效', README:47-48 'First-boot password (must be changed!)'), so 'silently' is true of operator feedback/logging, not of the docs — but README:141, in the block README itself labels '(recommended)', shows `ADMIN_PASSWORD="change-me" ./llm-router-guard`, which against the persistent ./gateway.db of that same deployment form is precisely the ignored, unwarned case. CORRECTIONS TO THE IMPACT NARRATIVE (they reduce scope, not validity): (i) claims (1) and (3) cannot both fire in one chain — editing .env and re-running `docker compose up -d` is itself the re-create that wipes /app/gateway.db, so bootstrap then applies the NEW password (data loss instead of stale password), whereas `docker restart` / host reboot keeps the writable layer (compose:27 `restart: unless-stopped`) and keeps the old hash; (ii) after a re-create the instance is empty, so 'compromise of all upstream provider keys' is delayed until the operator re-provisions without rotating, not immediate; (iii) the cross-reference phrasing 'authn-3/authn-4 (no login throttling)' is imprecise — throttling exists (auth.go:113-122) but is per-account and non-atomic (authn-4); (iv) an additional fact the original auditor missed strengthens the finding: the runtime image never ships the SPA (Dockerfile:26 copies only `/out/server`; there is no go:embed anywhere in backend/), so MountStatic auto-detect fails and returns at routes.go:165-167 without registering NoRoute → GET / is 404 under compose, and the documented remediation 'Change it immediately via the web UI' (README:56) is unreachable — an operator following quickstart §4 has neither an alert nor a UI to fix admin123. Net: default credential live + no log + no enforcement + no reachable remediation + network-published port = administrative account takeover by provisioning defect, which the rubric places at high. It is not critical because exploitation requires the operator to be on the default path (an accepted published default), not a code-level authz bypass. Recommendation as filed is appropriate; add 'also fix Dockerfile so the runtime image ships web/dist' since the UI rotation path is currently broken.
exploit_sketch:
Path 1 — documented Docker default (no code needed, just run it): (a) operator follows quickstart.en.md §4 `cp .env.template .env` (which ships ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin123 at line 28) or skips .env entirely, then `docker compose up -d`; (b) container writes /app/gateway.db (outside the ./data mount), bcrypts 'admin123' (main.go:175) and logs only `[bootstrap] created admin user: admin` — no WARNING, because pass != "" (main.go:171); (c) attacker: `curl -s -XPOST http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/auth/login -d '{"username":"admin","password":"admin123"}'` → 200 + 24h admin JWT (auth.go:110/124; MFA skipped since u.MFAEnabled=false, auth.go:86); (d) with that JWT: `GET /api/admin/v1/providers` (upstream config), `POST /api/admin/v1/apikeys` (mint a gateway key → spend upstream quota / read every prompt+response via `GET /api/admin/v1/audit/calls`), `PUT /api/admin/v1/settings/security` (disable MFA globally), `POST /api/admin/v1/backups/restore`.
Path 2 — the ignore is undetectable: single-binary deploy (README:137-141) with an existing ./gateway.db; operator sets `ADMIN_PASSWORD=Str0ng-Pass…` and restarts; bootstrapAdmin counts 1 user and returns at main.go:168 with zero log output; login with admin123 still succeeds.
Path 3 — the silent revert: rotate the password via `PUT /api/admin/v1/auth/password`, later upgrade the image / `docker compose down && up -d`; the container layer (and /app/gateway.db) is gone, AutoMigrate rebuilds the schema, bootstrapAdmin recreates admin with the still-default compose value → admin123 is valid again; the only console evidence is main.go:183.

verification_notes.quote_accuracy: All quoted lines match the source verbatim. Two deviations: (1) the quoted main.go:172 omits its inline comment `// 仅在未设置环境变量时默认，首次启动后必须修改`; (2) the cited line number 166 points at the Count() call rather than the `if count > 0 { return }` decision at 167-168 (corrected_line = 167).

chain_tests.attacker_privilege: Attacker genuinely lacks admin privilege beforehand; admin123 is the only published default the finding relies on and the code never re-checks it at login.
chain_tests.input_trust: No untrusted input involved — the risk is configuration/provisioning, and every configuration default claimed was read in the actual file.
chain_tests.mitigation_elsewhere: No mitigation found. Searched for any consumer of cfg.AdminPassword, any admin-user create/reset endpoint, any default-credential check in warnInsecureDefaults or login, any VOLUME/abs-path DB default. Only the (bypassable, per-account) lockout and the old-password requirement on rotation exist.
chain_tests.counter_facts_recorded: Claims A and C are mutually exclusive within one compose flow (editing .env triggers the re-create that applies the new password), and a freshly re-created instance holds no provider keys yet, so claim C's stated impact is delayed rather than immediate.
